title: Berlin Heating Season - Quick Summary
items: **The Berlin heating period runs 1 October to 30 April.** It is a convention built from tenancy agreements and court decisions, not a line in a statute, which is why nobody can show you the law.

**A cold snap can start the duty early.** Three days in a row below 12 °C outside at 21:00 and heating is owed before October. In four of the last eleven autumns Berlin crossed that line in September, the earliest on 19 September.

**Between 06:00 and 24:00 the figures are 20 to 22 °C in living rooms and kitchens and 23 °C in bathrooms.** At night the floor drops, and that night figure is the contested one: Berlin tenant advice accepts 16 °C, other guidance says 18 °C.

**The tenant has to prove the flat was cold.** Measure in the middle of the room, about one metre above the floor, several times a day across several days, and write down the hour as well as the temperature.

**Report the defect in writing before you touch the rent.** Name the rooms, temperatures and hours, set a short deadline, and say that further rent is paid under reserve. A reduction taken at the wrong percentage becomes an arrears problem.

**Two quiet rights.** If your building has remotely readable meters and you are not sent monthly consumption information, you may cut your heating share by 3 per cent. Meters that cannot be read remotely must be replaced by 31 December 2026.
**Every Berlin district runs a free tenant advice service.** It is funded by the Senate and open to any tenant in that district. Take the printed log with you.
